common_name: Raspberry Delight Sage (Cold-Hardy Jamensis Hybrid Bush Sage)

planting.note: Set out container plants in spring in lean, well-drained soil in full sun; it tolerates colder winters than most autumn sage selections once established.

directions: Raspberry Delight was discovered by New Mexico plantsman David Salman at his Santa Fe nursery as a hybrid between Salvia greggii 'Furman's Red' and a high-altitude Salvia microphylla collected in central Arizona, combining the compact habit of autumn sage with extra winter toughness. Two-lipped, deep raspberry-red flowers cover the multi-branched, semi-woody mound from spring through fall, drawing hummingbirds with little care beyond an occasional trim. It later served as the microphylla-type parent behind the even hardier hybrid 'Windwalker Royal Red', bred by crossing it with the tender Mexican species Salvia darcyi. Grow it in full sun and lean, well-drained soil with minimal supplemental water, and cut the woody framework back in late winter to keep growth dense.

common_name: Clear Sky Passionflower (Tetraploid Cold-Hardy Blue Passion Vine)

planting.note: Plant container vines after the last frost against a sturdy trellis or fence in full sun and well-drained soil.

directions: Bred by German Passiflora breeder Dr. Roland Fischer around 2001, Clear Sky is a robust tetraploid selection of blue passionflower prized for larger flowers, extra vigor, and improved cold tolerance compared to typical seed-grown Passiflora caerulea. Pale sky-blue and white petals surround a showy corona of blue-and-white banded filaments, opening in flushes from early summer into fall on a fast-climbing, semi-evergreen vine. It has since been used as a breeding parent, crossed with Passiflora loefgrenii 'Iporanga' to produce the widely admired hybrid 'Betty Myles Young'. Established plants tolerate brief hard frosts by dying back to the roots and resprouting vigorously the following spring.

common_name: Eichler's Passionflower (Brazilian Atlantic Forest Passion Vine)

planting.note: Plant in a warm, sheltered site with a trellis or fence after all frost danger has passed.

directions: Passiflora eichleriana is a semi-herbaceous, tendril-climbing passionflower native to the Atlantic Forest and Cerrado regions of southern and southeastern Brazil and neighboring Paraguay, scrambling over shrubs and fences rather than developing the thick woody stems of some larger Passiflora species. It carries the typical fringed coronal filaments of the genus and has been used by breeders as a parent species; crossed with the hardy Constance Eliott selection of blue passionflower, it contributed to the vigorous tetraploid hybrid 'White Wedding'. In cultivation it wants a warm, sheltered site with a trellis or fence to climb, full sun to light shade, and consistently moist but well-drained soil. Like most subtropical Passiflora, it is not reliably cold-hardy and benefits from winter protection outside the warmest zones.

common_name: Tucuman Passionflower (Fragrant Cold-Hardy Argentine Passion Vine)

planting.note: Plant against a trellis or fence in full sun after the last frost; roots survive cold winters even where top growth is killed back.

directions: Native to the Tucuman region of northern Argentina, Passiflora tucumanensis produces small, nodding, lightly fragrant flowers in loose succession, valued by breeders more for its fragrance and unusual cold hardiness than for size or show. It reportedly survives temperatures down to about 14 degrees Fahrenheit, making it nearly as cold-hardy as native maypop and a useful parent for breeding hardier passionflower hybrids, including a cross with maypop that produced 'Guglielmo Betto'. The vine climbs by tendrils into vigorous, semi-herbaceous growth each season, dying back in cold winters and regrowing from hardy roots. Grow it in full sun on a trellis or fence with well-drained soil, and expect light, sweetly scented flowers through the warm months rather than the large, showy blooms of tropical passionflower species.

common_name: Iporanga Garlic Passionflower (Rare Brazilian Large-Flowered Selection)

planting.note: Plant in a warm, frost-free site with a trellis or fence after the last frost, since this tropical selection has no cold tolerance.

directions: Collected near Brazil's Intervales Biological Reserve in Sao Paulo state, Iporanga is a rare, large-flowered selection of Passiflora loefgrenii, the species sometimes called garlic passion fruit for the pungent scent of its crushed foliage and fruit. Its blooms are considerably larger and more dramatic than those of the related 'Corupa' selection, opening flat to attract bees before reflexing sharply backward later in the day to suit visiting hummingbirds. The clone sets fruit poorly even with compatible pollen nearby, so it is grown chiefly as an ornamental and as a potent pollen parent in hybridizing, having contributed to the celebrated hybrid 'Betty Myles Young' when crossed with Passiflora 'Clear Sky' in 2005. As a tropical Brazilian species it needs warm, frost-free conditions, a trellis or fence to climb, full sun to bright part shade, and evenly moist, well-drained soil.
